summary: Brick tower first lit February 1850 on Nantucket's eastern bluff. Coskata crew rescued seven men in 1892; moved 405 feet inland in 2007 as erosion ate the bluff.

lens.where: A Fresnel lens was removed to the Nantucket Whaling Museum in 1938, and another Fresnel lens was removed in 1950; the nomination does not say whether these were one lens or two.

structures.note: Constructed 1849-50. The nomination gives 60 feet; LighthouseFriends describes a brick section of 53 feet with a granite section above it.
Brick oil house, 8 feet 6 inches square, recorded in the Board's report for fiscal 1892.

access.note: Grounds open daily from dawn until dusk. The 'Sconset Trust opens the tower for tours in June and October by reservation.

events.note: Brick tower constructed 1849-50 under Benjamin F. Isherwood's direction; cost $10,333 (nomination).
Second-order Fresnel lens from Henry-Lepaute of Paris (LighthouseFriends); the nomination says it was bought in France.
Dwelling for the assistant keeper built (LighthouseFriends).
Brick oil house built (Board, fiscal year ended 30 June 1892). The nomination and the USLHS record date the oil house to 1887; LighthouseFriends gives 1892.

Coskata station crew rescued seven men from the rigging of the British schooner H. P. Kirkham. The wreck table lists the Kirkham against Coskata, dated 20 January. The services table gives Rose and Crown Shoal, about fifteen miles from the station; the awards list gives 21 January 1892. The award counts twenty-three hours of battling wind and sea; LighthouseFriends counts twenty-six hours from setting off to landing.
Fire about a quarter of a mile north of the station, burned about 80 acres; keeper and assistant helped preserve lighthouse property (Bulletin 1920).
Electric light replaced the kerosene vapour light; candlepower from 99,000 to 720,000; assistant keeper's post eliminated. The Bulletin gives 14 May; LighthouseFriends gives 15 May.
Fresnel lens removed to the Nantucket Whaling Museum (nomination).
Fresnel lens removed (nomination); LighthouseFriends says it was replaced by rotating aerobeacons.
The 1887 keepers' duplex torn down and replaced with two one-story houses (LighthouseFriends).
Light automated (USLHS; LighthouseFriends); personnel lived at the station until 1992 (LighthouseFriends).
The 1991 storm tore away large pieces of the bluff (LighthouseFriends).
Tower moved 405 feet to a spot 250 feet from the edge of the bluff ('Sconset Trust). LighthouseFriends gives 390 feet to the northwest.
Oil house dated 1887 (nomination; USLHS record). The Board's FY1892 report and LighthouseFriends date a brick oil house to 1892.

The wreck table lists her against the Coskata station, 20 January 1892; the services table gives Rose and Crown Shoal, about fifteen miles from the station; the awards list gives 21 January 1892. Crew of seven rescued from the rigging by the Coskata station crew; keeper Walter N. Chase awarded a gold medal dated 2 April 1892.

resolved_conflicts.field: wrecks/H. P. Kirkham place and date
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1892 wreck table lists the H. P. Kirkham against Coskata, dated 20 January (OCR interleaves the columns; the row was matched by position). The services table gives Rose and Crown Shoal, about fifteen miles from the station; the awards list gives 21 January 1892. Both are reported in the story.
The Board's FY1892 report records a brick oil house built at Sankaty Head; LighthouseFriends gives 1892; the nomination and the USLHS record give 1887. The story states the disagreement.
The Sconset Trust gives 405 feet for the 2007 move; LighthouseFriends gives 390 feet. Both are stated.

notes_for_editor: FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22 (independent check; story and this record revised). UNRESOLVED CONFLICTS: (1) Lens: the nomination records a Fresnel lens removed to the Nantucket Whaling Museum in 1938 and another removed in 1950; it does not say whether these are one lens or two. LighthouseFriends mentions only the 1950 removal. (2) Tower height: nomination 60 feet; LighthouseFriends brick section 53 feet plus a granite section six feet; the record has 21.0 m. (3) Oil house: the Board's FY1892 report (scan p.391) records a brick oil house built at Sankaty Head; the nomination ('Today, a tower (1849), oil house (1887)') and the USLHS record ('Other Structures: OIL HOUSE (1887)') date it to 1887; LighthouseFriends says 1892. The story states the disagreement. An earlier note said the nomination gave no 1887 oil house; the nomination text read does give 1887. (4) Electrification: the 1933 Bulletin gives 14 May; LighthouseFriends gives 15 May. (5) Larsen: the roster has him as principal keeper until 1944; LighthouseFriends says he retired in December 1943. The story gives both. (6) Contractor and engineer: the nomination says Benjamin F. Isherwoode directed construction; LighthouseFriends names Cabet King as contractor; the roster lists a contractor Benjamin R. Isherwood with no dates. The roster line is not linked to the engineer. (7) Materials: LighthouseFriends says supplies were landed at Nantucket Harbor and carried across the island; the nomination (OCR reads 'bought', probably 'brought') says they came to the site by ship. (8) Relocation: the Sconset Trust gives 405 feet; LighthouseFriends gives 390 feet to the northwest. Both are in the story. (9) H. P. Kirkham, 1892: the wreck table (scan p.85) reads 'Br. sc. H. P. Kirk- Coskata, Massachusetts- ham. Jan 20' in OCR. The table's columns are interleaved in the OCR and the row was matched by position; 'Coskata, Massachusetts' may name the station column, not the place of the wreck, so the story says the table lists the schooner against the Coskata station. The services table (same page, OCR) gives 'Aground on Rose and Crown Shoal, fifteen miles from the life-saving station'; the table's place column gives 'fifteen and one-half miles'. The awards list (scan page not pinned) gives 'fifteen miles from Coskata Station, Nantucket, Mass., Jan. 21, 1892'. The award's phrase 'the crew of seven men from the rigging' is printed with medal columns interleaved in the OCR; it is quoted as printed. (10) Durations: the award says 'battling for twenty-three hours'; LighthouseFriends says twenty-six hours from setting off to landing. (11) Remsen's South Shoals Lightship dates are not given; the lightship is not matched to a station id. (12) George E. Dolby (Bulletin 1932 obituary, Cape Cod second assistant) is not linked to the roster's James E. Dolby (first assistant 1924 to 1933). (13) Larsen's Minot's Ledge, Cape Ann and The Graves service has no role or dates in LighthouseFriends; not recorded as roster lines. (14) USLHS place match by name and position (0.12 km). (15) LF-ONLY FACTS, no primary record read: the 1848 appropriation, the 1852 and 1853 Board reports (second-hand through LighthouseFriends), Cabet King, the Remsen and Larsen career details, the 1892 phone call, the 1953 duplex, the 1991 storm, the Save Our Sankaty group, Drake's 1875 visit. (16) The 1864 Board rules are general period context, marked in the story; they are quoted as the general rules for keepers, not as a Sankaty record. (17) SEARCH: Chronicling America hits for 'Sankaty' were unrelated; 'Coskata' with 'Kirkham' in Massachusetts papers, 1892, returned no hits. No newspaper material is used. (18) Keepers after 1950: the roster lists keepers and Coast Guard crews into the 1960s; kept as archive lines, not named in the story. The current keeper named on the Trust's site is not named here.
